paragraphs: We are a clinical-stage biotechnology company focused on developing precision therapies for genetically defined diseases. Our approach is to design rational precision therapies that treat the underlying cause of disease and improve the lives of patients. Our most advanced program is bezuclastinib, also known as CGT9486, a highly selective tyrosine kinase inhibitor that is designed to potently inhibit the KIT D816V mutation as well as other mutations in KIT exon 17. In the vast majority of cases, KIT D816V is responsible for driving Systemic Mastocytosis ("SM"), a serious and rare disease caused by unchecked proliferation of mast cells. Exon 17 mutations are also found in patients with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors ("GIST"), a type of cancer with strong dependence on oncogenic KIT signaling. Bezuclastinib is a highly selective and potent KIT inhibitor with the potential to provide a new treatment option for these patient populations. We are developing bezuclastinib to treat patients living with Non-Advanced Systemic Mastocytosis ("NonAdvSM"), Advanced Systemic Mastocytosis ("AdvSM") and GIST, and in 2025 we reported positive top-line results from registrational trials in each of these indications. We are building an internal commercial organization and expect to launch bezuclastinib commercially in the United State in the second half of 2026, pending regulatory approval. We also have an ongoing Phase 1 study of our novel internally developed FGFR2/3 inhibitor and have initiated a Phase 1 study of our CNS-penetrant, selective mutant ErbB2 inhibitor. In addition, the Cogent Research Team is developing a portfolio of novel targeted therapies to help patients fighting serious, genetically driven diseases targeting mutations in PI3Kα, KRAS and JAK2.

We have assembled a management team with extensive experience in the research, development, manufacturing and commercialization of pharmaceutical products, specifically including numerous successful precision medicines for genetically defined diseases. With the support of our board of directors and their expertise, we believe that the Company is well positioned to develop and commercialize novel precision medicines. Beginning with bezuclastinib, our mission is to develop and commercialize pharmaceutical products that improve the lives of patients fighting rare, genetically driven diseases.

Our vision is to discover, develop, and commercialize best-in-class therapies that have a meaningful impact for patients with genetically defined diseases. The principal components of our strategy include:
• Advance bezuclastinib toward regulatory approval and, if approved, commercialize the product in the United States and select international markets for patients with SM and GIST;

• Evaluate potential collaborations, partnerships, and licensing opportunities that could enhance the value of our existing programs and enable us to leverage the capabilities of strategic partners, including in geographies where partners can provide local expertise or operational scale;
• Explore the clinical utility of CGT4859, our selective and potent FGFR2/3 inhibitor, CGT4255, our CNS-penetrant, selective mutant ErbB2 inhibitor and CGT6297, our selective PI3Kα inhibitor; and
• Advance our JAK2 and KRAS preclinical programs, as well as our other undisclosed preclinical programs.

Bezuclastinib is designed to target mutations within the KIT receptor tyrosine kinase, including KIT D816V. As a Type I inhibitor, bezuclastinib is designed to selectively bind the active conformation of mutant KIT. In preclinical studies, bezuclastinib has demonstrated comparable potency relative to other FDA-approved KIT mutant inhibitors, and clear selectivity for KIT mutations versus other kinase targets frequently associated with other KIT inhibitors including, but not limited to PDGFRα, PDGFRβ, VEGFR2, FLT3, CSF1R and KDR. In preclinical studies of bezuclastinib, limited blood-brain-barrier penetration was observed, and there have been no clinically significant CNS toxicities identified. This preclinical profile of selectivity against kinases that have been associated with off-target toxicities and limited blood-brain-barrier penetration differentiate bezuclastinib from other KIT mutant inhibitors, and support the potential for a best-in-class clinical profile.

We licensed the exclusive worldwide rights to develop and commercialize bezuclastinib from Plexxikon Inc., a Daiichi Sankyo subsidiary ("Plexxikon"). Under the terms of the license agreement, Plexxikon received an upfront payment and is eligible for additional development and regulatory milestone payments along with mid- to high- single-digit royalty payments. We are developing bezuclastinib in both SM and GIST.

SM is driven by KIT D816V mutations causing a perpetual ‘on' state within mast cells, a type of white blood cell, leading to proliferation and accumulation in various internal organs and bone marrow. Key biomarkers of SM include but are not limited to, elevated serum tryptase, high mast cell burden in bone marrow and the KIT D816V variant allele frequency. As a highly selective and potent KIT inhibitor, bezuclastinib has the potential to provide a new treatment option for patients with SM. SM occurs when mast cells inappropriately accumulate in various internal organs in the body. Approximately 90% of SM patients present with NonAdvSM and 10% of patients present with AdvSM, a rare and very aggressive form of SM. There are three subtypes of AdvSM: aggressive SM ("ASM"), SM with associated hematologic neoplasm ("SM-AHN") and mast cell leukemia ("MCL").

Based on the characteristics of bezuclastinib, we are pursuing development of the compound in both patients with AdvSM and patients with NonAdvSM, the vast majority of whom have a KIT D816V mutation. Emerging clinical data for other kinase inhibitors with activity against KIT D816V have shown that SM patients are highly sensitive to inhibition of the target. Bezuclastinib was specifically designed to selectively inhibit KIT mutations, including KIT D816V.

SUMMIT is our registration-directed randomized, global, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multi-part Phase 2 clinical trial for patients with NonAdvSM. The study is designed to explore the safety and efficacy of bezuclastinib in patients

with moderate to severe NonAdvSM, which includes Indolent Systemic Mastocytosis ("ISM"), Smoldering Systemic Mastocytosis ("SSM") and Bone Marrow Mastocytosis. APEX is our registration-directed global, open-label, multi-center, Phase 2 clinical trial in patients with AdvSM evaluating the safety, efficacy, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic profiles of bezuclastinib.

We reported top-line results from our SUMMIT trial in July 2025 and full results in December 2025, as well as top-line results from our APEX trial in December 2025, all of which were positive and achieved all primary and key secondary endpoints. We submitted the first New Drug Application ("NDA") for bezuclastinib in patients with NonAdvSM in December 2025 and expect to submit an NDA in the first half of 2026 for patients with AdvSM. In October 2025, the FDA granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation for bezuclastinib in NonAdvSM patients previously treated with avapritinib as well as in patients with SSM, both patient populations with no currently approved standard of care. The FDA and European Medicines Agency ("EMA") have granted orphan drug designation to bezuclastinib for the treatment of Mastocytosis. In 2025, we initiated an expanded access program in the United States to allow eligible SM patients to receive investigational bezuclastinib prior to potential regulatory approval. Pending regulatory approval, we expect to launch bezuclastinib commercially in the United States in the second half of 2026 to treat patients with NonAdvSM.

headings: Risks Related to our Business
We face significant competition from other biotechnology and pharmaceutical companies, and our operating results will suffer if we fail to compete effectively.

The commercial success of any future approved drugs, including bezuclastinib, will depend upon the degree of market acceptance by physicians, patients, third-party payors, and others in the medical community.
A variety of risks associated with marketing our product candidates internationally could materially adversely affect our business.
If product liability lawsuits are brought against us, we may incur substantial liabilities and may be required to limit commercialization of bezuclastinib or any of our other product candidates.

Information obtained from expanded access studies may not reliably predict the efficacy of our future product candidates in company-sponsored clinical trials and may lead to adverse events that could limit approval.
Clinical trials are expensive, time-consuming, and difficult to design and implement.
If unacceptable side effects are identified during the development of our drug candidates, we may need to abandon or limit such development.
If difficulties arise enrolling patients in our clinical trials, clinical development activities could be delayed or otherwise adversely affected.

Since the number of patients that we have dosed to date in some of our clinical trials is small, the results from such clinical trials may be less reliable than results achieved in larger clinical trials.
We may choose not to develop a potential product candidate, or we may suspend, deprioritize or terminate one or more discovery programs or preclinical or clinical product candidates or programs.
We may form or seek collaborations or strategic alliances or enter into additional licensing arrangements in the future, but we may not realize any resulting benefits.
Risks Related to Our Reliance on Third Parties

The third parties upon whom we rely for the supply of the API and drug product used in bezuclastinib are our sole source of supply, and the loss of any of these suppliers could significantly harm our business.
Risks Related to Regulatory Approval of Our Drug Candidates and Other Legal Compliance Matters

Breakthrough Therapy Designation for bezuclastinib and our other product candidates or participation in the FDA's Real-Time Oncology Review ("RTOR") program may not lead to a faster development or review process.
The FDA regulatory approval process is lengthy and time-consuming, and we may experience significant delays in the clinical development and regulatory approval of our product candidates.
Regulatory authorities, including the FDA, may disagree with our regulatory plan and we may fail to obtain regulatory approval of our product candidates.

Obtaining and maintaining regulatory approval of our product candidates in one jurisdiction does not mean that we will be successful in obtaining regulatory approval of our product candidates in other jurisdictions.

Evolving regulatory standards, including as a result of changes in government leadership, make it difficult to accurately predict the likelihood of marketing approval even when clinical trials meet their endpoints.

Even if we receive regulatory approval for any investigational product, we will be subject to ongoing regulatory obligations and continued regulatory review, which may result in significant additional expense.
The impact of healthcare legislation and other changes in the healthcare industry and in healthcare spending on us is currently unknown, and may adversely affect our business model.
paragraphs: The following risk factors and other information included in this Annual Report on Form 10-K should be carefully considered. The risks and uncertainties described below are not the only ones we face. Additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we presently deem less significant may also impair our business operations. You should carefully consider the risks described below, as well as the other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including our financial statements and the related notes and "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations," as well as our other filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission, before deciding whether to invest in our common stock. If any of the following risks occur, our business, financial condition, results of operations and future growth prospects could be materially and adversely affected. Moreover, some of the factors, events and contingencies discussed below may have occurred in the past, but the disclosures below are not representations as to whether or not the factors, events or contingencies have occurred in the past and instead reflect our beliefs and opinions as to the factors, events, or contingencies that could materially and adversely affect us in the future. References to past events are provided by way of example only and are not intended to be a complete listing or a representation as to whether or not such factors have occurred in the past.

Our business is highly dependent on the success of our bezuclastinib program and our ability to discover and develop additional product candidates. We may not be successful in our efforts to develop bezuclastinib or expand our pipeline of drug candidates.

Our business and future success depend on our ability to develop, obtain regulatory approval for and then successfully commercialize bezuclastinib and any other product candidates that we may discover and develop. We are pursuing clinical development of bezuclastinib to target SM and GIST through our APEX, SUMMIT and PEAK clinical trials. We submitted the first New Drug Application ("NDA") for NonAdvSM in 2025; we initiated our NDA submission for GIST in January 2026 and expect to complete the submission in April 2026; and we plan to submit an NDA in AdvSM in the first half of 2026. There is no guarantee that bezuclastinib will be approved for any or all of these indications. Even if approved, bezuclastinib will require substantial investment, access to sufficient commercial manufacturing capacity and significant marketing efforts before we are able to generate any revenue from product sales, if ever.

Through the development of the research team, we are also working to build a pipeline of other product candidates. Researching, developing, obtaining regulatory approval for and commercializing additional product candidates will require substantial additional funding and is prone to the risks of failure inherent in medical product development. Even if we are successful in continuing to build and expand our pipeline, we cannot provide you any assurance that we will be able to successfully advance any of these additional product candidates through the development process, or that any such product candidates will be successfully commercialized, widely accepted in the marketplace or more effective than other commercially available alternatives.

The development and commercialization of new pharmaceutical and biotechnology products is highly competitive. We face competition with respect to bezuclastinib and our other product candidates and will face competition with respect to any drug candidates that we may seek to develop or commercialize in the future, from major pharmaceutical companies, specialty pharmaceutical companies, and biotechnology companies worldwide. There are a number of large pharmaceutical and biotechnology companies that currently market and sell products or are pursuing the development of products for the treatment of the disease indications for which we are developing our drug candidates. Potential competitors also include academic institutions, government agencies, and other public and private research organizations that conduct research, seek patent protection, and establish collaborative arrangements for research, development, manufacturing, and commercialization.

Any product candidates that we successfully develop and commercialize will compete with currently approved therapies and new therapies that may become available in the future from segments of the pharmaceutical, biotechnology and other related markets that pursue precision medicines. Our commercial opportunity could also be reduced or eliminated if our competitors develop and commercialize additional products that are safer, more effective, have superior dosing regimens, have fewer or less severe side effects, are approved for broader indications or patient populations, are approved for specific sub-populations, are more convenient or are less expensive than bezuclastinib or any other products that we may develop. Our competitors also may obtain FDA or other marketing approval for their products more rapidly than any approval we may obtain for ours, which could result in our competitors establishing a strong market position before we are able to enter the market. In addition, our ability to compete may be affected in many cases by insurers or other third-party payors seeking to encourage the use of generic products.

In addition, in 2025, we initiated an expanded access program in the United States to allow eligible SM patients to receive investigational bezuclastinib prior to potential regulatory approval.

We are also pursuing the development of bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib as a potential second line treatment for patients living with GIST. GIST is a cancer frequently driven by KIT mutations, and resistance to currently available therapeutics is frequently associated with the emergence of other KIT mutations. First-line therapy for the vast majority of GIST patients is imatinib, followed by sunitinib monotherapy as the current second-line therapy for the majority of patients that eventually develop resistance to imatinib.

PEAK is our randomized open-label, global Phase 3 clinical trial designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib compared to sunitinib alone in patients with locally advanced, unresectable or metastatic GIST who have received prior treatment with imatinib. We announced positive top-line results from PEAK in November 2025, which demonstrated a substantial and highly statistically significant clinical benefit on the primary endpoint of progression free survival ("PFS"). Median PFS was 16.5 months for the bezuclastinib combination vs. 9.2 months for sunitinib monotherapy, and the bezuclastinib combination reduced the risk of disease progression or death by 50% compared to sunitinib monotherapy. In January 2026, we announced that the FDA agreed to accept our NDA for bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib for patients with GIST who have received prior treatment with imatinib under the Real-Time Oncology Review ("RTOR") program, and shortly thereafter we initiated our NDA submission to FDA under this program. We expect to complete the GIST NDA submission in April 2026. In January 2026, the FDA also granted Breakthrough Therapy Designation ("BTD") for bezuclastinib in combination with sunitinib for patients with GIST who have received prior treatment with imatinib. Bezuclastinib has been granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of GIST by the FDA and under the Orphan Drug Act and the European Medicines Agency ("EMA").

In mid-2026, we expect to initiate a Phase 2 trial investigating the benefit of the bezuclastinib plus sunitinib combination for first-line GIST patients with exon 9 mutations who are naive to, or recently initiated treatment with, imatinib.

In 2025, we initiated an expanded access program in the United States for patients affected with advanced, metastatic, and/or unresectable GIST, intolerant to imatinib or received prior imatinib therapy for treatment that resulted in disease progression, and who meet other inclusion and exclusion criteria.

Worldwide rights to develop and commercialize bezuclastinib are exclusively licensed from Plexxikon Inc., a member of the Daiichi Sankyo Group ("Plexxikon"). Under the terms of the license agreement, Plexxikon received an upfront payment and is eligible for additional development milestones of up to $7.5 million upon the satisfaction of certain clinical milestones and up to $25.0 million upon the satisfaction of certain regulatory milestones. During the second quarter of 2022, as a result of the progression of the PEAK study, the first clinical milestone was achieved, resulting in payment of $2.5 million to Plexxikon in June 2022. In the fourth quarter of 2025, $5.0 million became payable on achievement of regulatory milestones and another $15.0 million may become payable in the next twelve months as a result of achievement of additional regulatory milestones.

Patents protecting bezuclastinib include composition of matter claims which have been issued in the United States and other key territories and provide exclusivity through 2033 and potentially beyond through patent term extensions. In addition, we have pending patent applications in the United States and other key territories that seeks to protect our optimized formulation of bezuclastinib, which could potentially provide exclusivity through at least 2043, as well as a pending U.S. provisional patent application directed to methods of administering bezuclastinib, which could potentially provide exclusivity through at least 2046.

paragraphs: 本公司為一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於開發針對遺傳定義疾病之精準療法。我們的作法是設計合理的精準療法，以治療疾病的根源並改善病患的生活品質。我們目前最進展的計畫為 bezuclastinib，也稱為 CGT9486，為一種高度選擇性的酪胺酸激酶抑制劑，設計用以強效抑制 KIT D816V 突變以及 KIT exon 17 的其他突變。在絕大多數情況下，KIT D816V 是導致全身性肥大細胞症（"SM"）的主因，此為一種嚴重且罕見的疾病，由肥大細胞無限制增殖所引起。exon 17 突變也見於進階型胃腸間質瘤（"GIST"）病患，此為一種癌症，對致癌性 KIT 信號有強烈依賴。bezuclastinib 為一種高度選擇性且強效的 KIT 抑制劑，有潛力為這些病患族羣提供新的治療選擇。我們正在開發 bezuclastinib 用以治療患有非進階型全身性肥大細胞症（"NonAdvSM"）、進階型全身性肥大細胞症（"AdvSM"）以及 GIST 的病患，並於 2025 年報告了在這些適應症中註冊試驗的正面初步結果。我們正在建立內部的商業團隊，預計在 2026 年第二季於美國商業上市 bezuclastinib，待取得監管批准為止。我們也進行一項關於我們自行開發的新型 FGFR2/3 抑制劑的 Phase 1 研究，並已啟動一項關於我們 CNS 穿透性、選擇性突變 ErbB2 抑制劑的 Phase 1 研究。此外，Cogent 研究團隊正在開發一組新型的標的治療藥物，以協助與嚴重、遺傳驅動疾病抗戰的病患，針對 PI3Kα、KRAS 和 JAK2 的突變。
我們已組建了一支具備豐富經驗的管理團隊，專門在藥物產品的研究、開發、製造與商業化領域，特別包括許多成功之針對遺傳定義疾病的精準藥物。在董事會及其專業知識的支持下，我們相信本公司有優勢可開發與商業化新型精準藥物。從 bezuclastinib 開始，我們的使命是開發與商業化能改善與罕見、遺傳驅動疾病抗戰的病患生活品質的藥物產品。
我們的願景是發現、開發與商業化最佳等級的療法，對患有遺傳定義疾病的病患產生有意義的影響。我們策略的主要零組件包括：
• 推動 bezuclastinib 向監管批准進展，若獲批准，則於美國及選擇性的國際市場商業上市，用以治療 SM 與 GIST 病患；
• 評估潛在的合作、夥伴關係與授權機會，以提升我們現有計畫的價值，並使我們能利用策略夥伴的能力，包括在夥伴可提供當地專業知識或運營規模的地理區域；
• 探索 CGT4859（我們的選擇性且強效 FGFR2/3 抑制劑）、CGT4255（我們的 CNS 穿透性、選擇性突變 ErbB2 抑制劑）與 CGT6297（我們的選擇性 PI3Kα 抑制劑）的臨牀效益；以及
• 推動我們的 JAK2 與 KRAS 前臨牀計畫，以及我們其他未公開的前臨牀計畫。

bezuclastinib 設計用以針對 KIT 受體酪胺酸激酶中的突變，包括 KIT D816V。作為一種 Type I 抑制劑，bezuclastinib 設計用以選擇性地與突變 KIT 的活化構象結合。在前臨牀研究中，bezuclastinib 顯示出與其他 FDA 批准的 KIT 突變抑制劑相當的強效，並對 KIT 突變與其他常與其他 KIT 抑制劑相關的激酶目標有明確的選擇性，包括但不限於 PDGFRα、PDGFRβ、VEGFR2、FLT3、CSF1R 和 KDR。在 bezuclastinib 的前臨牀研究中，觀察到有限的血腦屏障穿透力，且未發現臨牀上顯著的 CNS 毒性。這種對與脫標毒性相關的激酶的選擇性以及有限的血腦屏障穿透力的前臨牀特性，使 bezuclastinib 與其他 KIT 突變抑制劑有所區別，並支持其潛在的最佳等級臨牀表現。

本公司取得 Plexxikon Inc.，為 Daiichi Sankyo 旗下公司（"Plexxikon"）獨家全球開發與商業化 bezuclastinib 的授權。根據授權協議的條款，Plexxikon 收到一筆 upfront payment，並有資格獲得額外的開發與監管里程碑付款，以及中單數字至高單數字的版稅付款。本公司正在 SM 與 GIST 兩種疾病中開發 bezuclastinib。

SM 是由 KIT D816V 突變導致肥大細胞持續處於 "on" 狀態，肥大細胞為一種白血球，導致其在各種內臟器官與骨髓中增殖與累積。SM 的關鍵生物標記包括但不限於，血清 tryptase 水準升高、骨髓中肥大細胞負荷高，以及 KIT D816V 突變等位基因頻率。作為一種高度選擇性且強效的 KIT 抑製劑，bezuclastinib 有潛力為 SM 患者提供新的治療選擇。SM 發生於肥大細胞不恰當地在體內各內臟器官中累積。約 90% 的 SM 患者為 NonAdvSM，10% 的患者為 AdvSM，為一種罕見且極具侵略性的 SM 病變。AdvSM 有三種亞型：侵略性 SM（"ASM"）、與血液學惡性腫瘤相關的 SM（"SM-AHN"）以及肥大細胞白血病（"MCL"）。
根據 bezuclastinib 的特性，本公司正在追求在 AdvSM 患者與 NonAdvSM 患者中開發此化合物，其中絕大多數患者具有 KIT D816V 突變。針對其他具有針對 KIT D816V 活性之激酶抑制劑的臨牀數據顯示，SM 患者對目標抑制具有高度敏感性。bezuclastinib 是特別設計用以選擇性抑制 KIT 突變，包括 KIT D816V。
SUMMIT 是本公司以註冊為導向的全球多中心雙盲安慰劑對照多階段 II 期臨牀試驗，用於治療 NonAdvSM 患者。該試驗設計用以探討 bezuclastinib 在中度至重度 NonAdvSM 患者中的安全性與有效性，包括惰性系統性肥大細胞症（"ISM"）、進行性系統性肥大細胞症（"SSM"）以及骨髓肥大細胞症。
APEX 是本公司以註冊為導向的全球開放標籤多中心 II 期臨牀試驗，用於治療 AdvSM 患者，評估 bezuclastinib 的安全性、有效性、藥動學與藥效學特徵。

本公司於 2025 年 7 月報告 SUMMIT 試驗的初步結果，並於 2025 年 12 月報告完整結果，同時於 2025 年 12 月報告 APEX 試驗的初步結果，所有結果皆為正面，並達成所有主要與關鍵次要終點。本公司於 2025 年 12 月提交 bezuclastinib 在 NonAdvSM 患者中的第一份新藥申請（"NDA"），並預計於 2026 年第一季提交 NDA，用以治療 AdvSM 患者。2025 年 10 月，美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）授予 bezuclastinib 在曾接受 avapritinib 治療的 NonAdvSM 患者以及 SSM 患者（兩者皆無現行核准標準治療）的突破性療法指定。FDA 與歐洲藥物管理局（"EMA"）已授予 bezuclastinib 治療肥大細胞症的罕見疾病藥物指定。2025 年，本公司在美國啟動擴展接觸計畫，允許符合資格的 SM 患者在潛在監管核准前接收到 investigational bezuclastinib。待監管核准後，本公司預計於 2026 年第二季在美國商業化 launch bezuclastinib，用以治療 NonAdvSM 患者。

paragraphs: 以下對我們財務狀況及營運成果的討論與分析，應與本年度10-K表報表末附的財務報表及相關附註一併閱讀。部分資訊包含在本年度10-K表報表中，包括有關我們商業計畫與策略的資訊，均為前瞻性陳述，涉及風險與不確定性。由於許多因素，包括本年度10-K表報表中「風險因素」部分所列因素，我們實際結果可能與以下討論與分析中所描述或暗示的前瞻性陳述結果有重大差異。以下討論呈現我們財務狀況及營運成果於會計年度2025與2024的資料。請參閱我們於2025年2月25日提交至SEC的會計年度2024年12月31日結業之10-K表報表，第II部第7項「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」，以取得有關會計年度2024年12月31日結業之財務狀況與營運成果，以及與會計年度2023年12月31日結業之比較資訊。

我們是一家臨牀階段的生物科技公司，專注於開發針對遺傳性疾病的精準療法。我們的策略是設計合理的精準療法，用以治療疾病的根源並改善病患的生活品質。我們最進展的計畫為bezuclastinib，也稱為CGT9486，是一種高度選擇性的酪胺酸 kinase 抑制劑，設計用以強效抑制KIT D816V變異以及KIT exon 17的其他變異。在絕大多數情況下，KIT D816V變異是導致系統性肥大細胞症（"SM"）的主因，這是一種嚴重且罕見的疾病，由肥大細胞不受控制的增殖所引起。exon 17的變異也出現在進階胃腸間質瘤（"GIST"）病患中，這是一種癌症，對致癌性KIT訊號有強烈依賴。Bezuclastinib是一種高度選擇性且強效的KIT抑制劑，有潛力為這些病患族羣提供新的治療選擇。我們正在開發bezuclastinib用以治療患有非進階性系統性肥大細胞症（"NonAdvSM"）、進階性系統性肥大細胞症（"AdvSM"）以及GIST的病患，並在2025年我們報告了在這些適應症中註冊試驗的正面初步結果。

我們認為bezuclastinib在這些適應症中代表著重要的商業機會。根據內部分析與外部市場研究，我們估計bezuclastinib與sunitinib組合作為GIST病患的潛在第二線治療，全球年度市場機會超過40億美元；約35億美元用以治療NonAdvSM病患；約5億美元用以治療AdvSM病患。我們正在建立內部的商業團隊，預計在2026年下半年於美國正式上市銷售bezuclastinib，待取得相關監管許可為止。
我們也進行了一項持續的Phase 1試驗，用以評估我們自行開發的FGFR2/3抑制劑，並已啟動一項Phase 1試驗，用以評估我們的CNS穿透性、選擇性突變ErbB2抑制劑。此外，Cogent研究團隊正在開發一系列的創新標的治療藥物，用以協助與嚴重、遺傳驅動疾病的病患，針對PI3Kα、KRAS及JAK2的變異進行治療。

SM是由KIT D816V變異所驅動，導致肥大細胞（一種白血球）持續處於「開」的狀態，導致在各種內臟器官與骨髓中增殖與累積。SM的關鍵生物標記包括但不限於，血清tryptase升高、骨髓中肥大細胞負荷高以及KIT D816V變異等位基因頻率。作為一種高度選擇性且強效的KIT抑制劑，bezuclastinib有潛力為SM病患提供新的治療選擇。SM發生在肥大細胞不恰當地在體內各內臟器官中累積的情況下。約有90%的SM病患為NonAdvSM，10%的病患為AdvSM，這是一種罕見且非常惡性的SM形式。AdvSM有三種亞型：侵略性SM（"ASM"）、與血液學惡性腫瘤相關的SM（"SM-AHN"）以及肥大細胞白血病（"MCL"）。

SUMMIT是我們用以註冊的隨機、全球、多中心、雙盲、安慰劑控制、多階段Phase 2臨牀試驗，用於治療NonAdvSM病患。該試驗設計用以評估bezuclastinib在中度至重度NonAdvSM病患中的安全性與有效性，包括緩和性系統性肥大細胞症（"ISM"）、進行性系統性肥大細胞症（"SSM"）以及骨髓肥大細胞症。APEX是我們用以註冊的全球、開放標籤、多中心、Phase 2臨牀試驗，用以評估bezuclastinib在AdvSM病患中的安全性、有效性、藥動學與藥效學特性。我們在2025年7月報告了SUMMIT試驗的初步結果，並在2025年12月報告了完整結果，同時也在2025年12月報告了APEX試驗的初步結果，所有結果均為正面，並達成所有主要與關鍵次要終點。

我們在2025年12月提交了bezuclastinib在NonAdvSM病患中的第一個新藥申請（"NDA"），並預計在2026年上半年提交NDA用以治療AdvSM病患。2025年10月，美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）授予bezuclastinib在曾接受avapritinib治療的NonAdvSM病患以及SSM病患中的突破性療法指定，這兩個病患族羣目前尚無核准的標準治療方案。美國食品藥物管理局（"FDA"）與歐洲藥物管理局（"EMA"）已授予bezuclastinib用以治療肥大細胞症的罕見病藥物指定。
此外，在2025年，我們在美國啟動了一個擴展准入計畫，允許符合資格的SM病患在潛在監管核准前接收到研究用的bezuclastinib。
本公司亦積極進行bezulcastinib與sunitinib組合之開發，作為治療患有胃腸間質瘤（GIST）患者之潛在第二線治療方案。GIST是一種常因KIT基因突變所驅動之癌症，且對現有治療藥物產生抗藥性，通常與其他KIT基因突變之出現有關。GIST患者大多數之首線治療為imatinib，隨後以sunitinib單藥治療作為大多數對imatinib產生抗藥性之患者之現行第二線治療方案。

PEAK為本公司設計之隨機開放標籤、全球第三期臨牀試驗，用以評估bezulcastinib與sunitinib組合在曾接受imatinib治療之局部晚期、無法手術切除或轉移性GIST患者中，與sunitinib單藥相比之安全性、耐受性及有效性。本公司於2025年11月宣佈PEAK試驗之初步結果為正向，顯示在主要評估指標「無疾病進展生存期（PFS）」上具有顯著且高度統計學意義之臨牀效益。bezulcastinib組合之中位PFS為16.5個月，而sunitinib單藥治療為9.2個月，且bezulcastinib組合相較於sunitinib單藥治療，將疾病進展或死亡風險降低50%。本公司於2026年1月宣佈美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）同意接受本公司針對曾接受imatinib治療之GIST患者之bezulcastinib與sunitinib組合之新藥申請（NDA），並在短時間內啟動根據實時癌症審查（RTOR）計畫向FDA提交NDA。本公司預期於2026年4月完成GIST NDA提交。本公司於2026年1月亦獲得FDA授予bezulcastinib與sunitinib組合之突破性治療指定（BTD），用於曾接受imatinib治療之GIST患者。FDA及歐洲藥品管理局（EMA）已授予bezulcastinib用於治療GIST之罕見疾病藥物指定（Orphan Drug Designation）。
預計於2026年中，本公司將啟動一項第二期試驗，研究bezulcastinib與sunitinib組合對未曾接受或近期開始接受imatinib治療之GIST患者之效益，這些患者具有exon 9基因突變。
於2025年，本公司在美國啟動了一項擴展接觸計畫，為患有晚期、轉移性及/或無法手術切除之GIST患者提供治療，這些患者對imatinib不耐受或曾接受imatinib治療但導致疾病進展，且符合其他入組與排除標準。

全球開發與商業化bezulcastinib之權利已由Plexxikon Inc.（為Daiichi Sankyo集團成員）獨佔授權。根據授權協議條款，Plexxikon已收到一筆預付金，並在達成特定臨牀里程碑時可獲得最高達750萬美元之額外開發里程碑付款，以及在達成特定監管里程碑時可獲得最高達2500萬美元之額外監管里程碑付款。於2022年第二季，因PEAK試驗進展，達成首個臨牀里程碑，於2022年6月支付Plexxikon 250萬美元。於2025年第四季，因達成監管里程碑，應支付500萬美元，且未來十二個月內可能因達成其他監管里程碑而再支付1500萬美元。
保護bezulcastinib之專利包括已發明之組成物專利，於美國及其他關鍵地區已發行，並提供至2033年及可能更長時間之獨佔權，透過專利期限延長。此外，本公司於美國及其他關鍵地區有待審查之專利申請，用以保護本公司優化之bezulcastinib製劑，可能提供至2043年之獨佔權，以及一項美國臨時專利申請，用以保護bezulcastinib之給藥方法，可能提供至2046年之獨佔權。

headings: 與我們業務相關的風險
我們面臨來自其他生物科技和製藥公司的激烈競爭，若我們無法有效競爭，將會導致我們的營運結果受損。
任何未來獲批准藥物的商業成功，包括 bezuclastinib，將取決於醫療專業人員、患者、第三方支付者及其他醫療界人士的市場接受度。
與國際市場我們產品候選藥物相關的多種風險，可能會對我們的業務造成重大不利影響。
若有人對我們提起產品責任訴訟，我們可能會面臨重大賠償責任，並可能被要求限制 bezuclastinib 或我們其他產品候選藥物的商業化。
來自擴展准入研究所獲得的資訊，可能無法可靠預測我們未來產品候選藥物在公司贊助臨牀試驗中的療效，並可能導致不良事件，從而限制核准。
臨牀試驗費用高昂、耗時且難以設計與執行。
若在藥物候選品的開發過程中發現無法接受的副作用，我們可能需要放棄或限制該開發。
若在進行臨牀試驗時遇到招募病患的困難，臨牀開發活動可能延遲或受到其他不利影響。
由於截至目前為止在一些臨牀試驗中接受治療的病患人數較少，因此這些臨牀試驗的結果可能不如在較大型臨牀試驗中取得的結果可靠。
本公司可能選擇不開發潛在的產品候選藥物，或可能暫停、降低優先順序或終止一個或多個發現計畫或臨牀前或臨牀產品候選藥物或計畫。
本公司未來可能成立或尋求合作夥伴或戰略聯盟，或與其他公司簽訂額外的授權協議，但本公司可能無法實現由此產生的任何好處。
與本公司依賴第三方之風險
本公司用於bezulcastinib的API及藥物產品之供應商為本公司唯一來源，若失去任何這些供應商，將可能對本公司業務造成重大影響。
與本公司藥物候選藥物之監管批准及其他法律合規事項相關之風險
bezulcastinib及本公司其他產品候選藥物之突破性療法指定或參與美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）之實時腫瘤審查（"RTOR"）計畫，可能不會導致開發或審查程序加速進行。
FDA 規管審批程序耗時且耗費大量時間，本公司可能面臨產品候選藥物臨牀開發及規管審批過程出現顯著延誤。
規管機關，包括 FDA，可能不同意本公司規管計畫，本公司可能無法取得產品候選藥物的規管審批。
在某一管轄區取得並維持產品候選藥物規管審批並不表示本公司將能在其他管轄區成功取得規管審批。
規管標準的變化，包括因政府領導層變動所導致的改變，使我們難以準確預測即使臨牀試驗達成其終點，仍可能取得市場核准的機率。
即使本公司取得任何 investigational product 的規管核准，本公司仍將面臨持續的規管義務及持續的規管審查，這可能會導致顯著的額外費用。
醫療保健法規的影響及其他醫療保健產業與醫療保健支出的變動對本公司目前尚屬未知，且可能對本公司商業模式產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 下列風險因素及其他資訊包含於本年度報告表 10-K 中，應謹慎考量。上述所描述的風險與不確定性並非我們所面臨的唯一風險。尚有其他風險與不確定性，目前我們尚未知悉或認為較不重要，也可能影響我們的業務運作。您應謹慎考量下列所描述的風險，以及本年度報告表 10-K 中的其他資訊，包括我們的財務報表及相關附註，以及「管理層對財務狀況與營運結果之討論與分析」，以及我們向證券交易委員會提交的其他申報文件，以決定是否投資本公司普通股。若任何上述風險發生，將可能對我們的業務、財務狀況、營運結果與未來成長前景造成重大且不利的影響。此外，部分所討論的因素、事件與潛在狀況可能已發生於過去，但下列披露並非表示這些因素、事件或潛在狀況是否已發生於過去，而是反映我們對可能對我們未來造成重大且不利影響的因素、事件或潛在狀況的信念與觀點。對過去事件的提及僅為範例，並非完整清單或表示這些因素是否已發生於過去。
我們的業務高度依賴 bezuclastinib 程式之成功，以及我們發現與開發其他產品候選物的能力。我們可能無法成功進行 bezuclastinib 的開發，或擴展我們的藥物候選物管道。

我們的業務與未來成功，取決於我們開發、取得相關監管批准，並成功商業化 bezuclastinib 及任何我們可能發現與開發的其他產品候選物的能力。我們正在進行 bezuclastinib 的臨牀開發，以針對 SM 與 GIST，透過 APEX、SUMMIT 與 PEAK 臨牀試驗。我們於 2025 年提交了第一份新藥申請（"NDA"）用於 NonAdvSM；我們於 2026 年 1 月啟動 GIST 的 NDA 申請，預計於 2026 年 4 月完成申請；我們計畫於 2026 年上半年提交 AdvSM 的 NDA。無法保證 bezuclastinib 會被批准用於任何或所有這些適應症。即使獲得批准，bezuclastinib 需要大量投資、足夠的商業製造能力與大量的市場推廣努力，才能在產生任何產品銷售收入之前，若有的話。
透過研究團隊的發展，我們也在努力建立其他產品候選物的管道。研究、開發、取得相關監管批准與商業化其他產品候選物，將需要大量額外資金，且醫療產品開發本身即具有失敗風險。即使我們成功持續建立與擴展我們的產品候選物管道，我們無法向您保證我們將能成功將任何這些其他產品候選物推進至開發過程，或任何這些產品候選物能成功商業化、在市場上廣受接受或比其他現有商業化替代品更有效。

新藥與生物技術產品的開發與商業化高度競爭。我們在 bezuclastinib 與其他產品候選物方面面臨競爭，未來若我們尋求開發或商業化任何藥物候選物，也會面臨來自全球大型藥品公司、專門藥品公司與生物技術公司的競爭。目前有許多大型藥品與生物技術公司正在市場銷售產品，或正在開發產品，用以治療我們正在開發藥物候選物的疾病適應症。潛在競爭者也包括大學機構、政府機構及其他公私立研究機構，這些機構進行研究、尋求專利保護，並建立合作關係，以進行研究、開發、製造與商業化。

我們成功開發與商業化任何產品候選物後，將與目前核准的治療方式及未來可能出現的新治療方式競爭，這些治療方式可能來自藥品、生物技術及其他相關市場中追求精準醫療的領域。我們的商業機會也可能因競爭對手開發與商業化更安全、更有效、劑量規程更佳、副作用較少或較輕微、核准適應症更廣或患者羣體更廣、核准特定子羣體、更便利或成本更低的產品而減少或消失。競爭對手也可能比我們更快獲得 FDA 或其他市場核准，這可能導致競爭對手在我們進入市場前已建立強大的市場地位。此外，我們的競爭能力在許多情況下可能受到保險公司或其他第三方支付者的影響，這些機構可能鼓勵使用通用藥物。
